data.content_ref: inline:SRC_005's 'epistemic tariff' mechanism contradicts SRC_001's 'self-reinforcing silo' mechanism on the direction of causal force: SRC_005 claims the tariff protects incumbent vocabulary from invalidation (outward defensive pressure), while SRC_001 claims silos never encounter anomalies forcing a bridge (inward isolation pressure). These are not the same mechanism: protection implies the rival primitive exists and is warded off, whereas siloing implies the rival primitive is never encountered at all. The contradiction holds when a lineage actively excludes known rivals (tariff) versus passively missing unknown rivals (silo). It is refuted if 'protection' and 'isolation' are formally identical operations in the allocation function, making the directional distinction a framing artifact rather than a mechanistic divergence.
